claim: mTORC1 activity, which leads to the phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 (pS6) via the activation of S6 kinase 1 (S6K1), was detectable in developing mouse retina but was absent in the neighboring retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and ciliary margin (CM).
source: mTORC1 activity, which leads to the phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6 (pS6) via the activation of S6 kinase 1 (S6K1), was detectable in developing mouse retina but was absent in the neighboring retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and CM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1, which visualizes pS6 staining patterns in different regions of the developing eye.

claim: The eyes of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice at P14 and P30 were significantly smaller than those of Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermates.
source: We found that the eyes of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice at P14 and P30 were significantly smaller than those of Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermates (Figure 1A and B, top rows)
evidence: The claim is supported by visual data in Figure 1A and B showing eye size comparisons, and quantitative measurements.

claim: The ciliary body (CB) and iris were malformed in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice.
source: and their ciliary body (CB) and iris were malformed (arrows in Figure 1A, middle row).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological images in Figure 1A showing structural abnormalities indicated by arrows.

claim: The Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas exhibited multiple rosette structures.
source: Moreover, the Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas exhibited multiple rosette structures (arrowheads in Figure 1A, bottom row).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological images in Figure 1A showing rosette structures indicated by arrowheads.

claim: The structural alterations in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas began after the first postnatal week.
source: However, these phenotypes were not observed in P7 Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse eyes (Figure 1A and B, two leftmost columns). The results suggest that the structural alterations in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas began after the first postnatal week.
evidence: The claim is based on temporal comparison of phenotypes at different developmental stages (P7 vs P14/P30) shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The loss of Müller glia (MG) is a major cause of retinal rosette formation.
source: It is known that the loss of MG is a major cause of retinal rosette formation (Willbold et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous literature (Willbold et al., 2000).

claim: The cells expressing MG markers were decreased significantly in P14 and P30 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared with Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate retinas.
source: We found that the cells expressing the MG markers, including p27, SRY-box transcription factors 2 and 9 (Sox2 and Sox9), and glutamine synthetase, were decreased significantly in P14 and P30 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared with Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate retinas, whereas the numbers of other retinal cell types were not significantly different in those two retinas (Figure 1C and D; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and quantification in Figure 1D, as well as supplementary data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The numbers of MG were increased in P7 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina.
source: However, the numbers of MG were rather increased in P7 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B); this is likely due to the developmental acceleration of MG production, as it was reported previously (Choi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, and is explained by reference to a previous publication (Choi et al., 2018).

claim: The numbers of apoptotic cells were elevated in the MG population of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The numbers of apoptotic cells, which were assessed by TUNEL (terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling) and immunostaining of cleaved active caspase-3 (Casp-3), were also elevated in the MG population of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B,C,D,E,F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL and caspase-3 immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-G.

claim: The apoptotic cells were enriched in the Tsc1-deficient cell population positive for the Cre reporter, ROSA26tdTomato (R26tdTom).
source: Furthermore, the apoptotic cells were enriched in the Tsc1-deficient cell population positive for the Cre reporter, ROSA26tdTomato (R26tdTom) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and C), suggesting that Tsc1 deletion had autonomous effects on MG degeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and C, demonstrating that apoptotic cells are predominantly in the Cre-affected population.

claim: Tsc1 deletion had autonomous effects on MG degeneration.
source: Furthermore, the apoptotic cells were enriched in the Tsc1-deficient cell population positive for the Cre reporter, ROSA26tdTomato (R26tdTom) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and C), suggesting that Tsc1 deletion had autonomous effects on MG degeneration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that apoptotic cells are enriched in Tsc1-deficient cells, suggesting cell-autonomous effects.

claim: Retinal rosettes and degeneration of MG were observed in Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice.
source: Retinal rosettes and degeneration of MG were also observed in Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice, in which the other TSC component, Tsc2 (Inoki et al., 2002; Saxton and Sabatini, 2017), was deleted in the RPE and CM cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and C, and references to literature (Inoki et al., 2002; Saxton and Sabatini, 2017) establishing Tsc2's role in the TSC complex.

claim: Eyes of Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice were not significantly different in size compared to those of Tsc2fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre mice.
source: However, eyes of Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice were not significantly different in size compared to those of Tsc2fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre mice, and their CB and iris were intact (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by eye size measurements and histological images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B.

claim: The microphthalmia and CB/iris malformation of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice is not due to mTORC1 hyperactivation.
source: These results suggest that the microphthalmia and CB/iris malformation of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice is not due to mTORC1 hyperactivation; instead, they might be caused by cellular events that are regulated by Tsc1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison between Tsc1 and Tsc2 deletion phenotypes, where Tsc2 deletion causes retinal rosettes but not microphthalmia/CB/iris defects.

claim: MG degeneration and retinal rosette formation were not observed in P30 Tsc1fl/fl;Slc1a3-CreERT2 mice when Tsc1 was deleted in MG beginning at P10 by tamoxifen injection.
source: However, we could not observe MG degeneration or retinal rosettes in P30 Tsc1fl/fl;Slc1a3-CreERT2 mice, from which Tsc1 was deleted in MG beginning at P10 by Tam injection (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 2A showing normal retinal structure in these mice.

claim: The retinal rosettes of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice were still evident when mTORC1 was inhibited by daily injection of rapamycin during the second postnatal week.
source: We also found that the retinal rosettes of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice were still evident when mTORC1 was inhibited by daily injection of a chemical inhibitor, rapamycin, during the second postnatal week (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 2B showing persistent rosettes despite rapamycin treatment.

claim: The numbers of MG in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were not recovered by rapamycin treatment.
source: The numbers of MG in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were also not recovered by rapamycin treatment, whereas pS6 was completely absent from the rapamycin-treated mouse retinas.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 2B showing persistent MG loss despite effective mTORC1 inhibition (absence of pS6).

claim: The degenerative phenotypes are not due to mTORC1 activation in the MG; instead, they likely arise from mTORC1 activation in the developing mouse retina.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that the degenerative phenotypes are not due to mTORC1 activation in the MG; instead, they likely arise from mTORC1 activation in the developing mouse retina.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observations that MG-specific Tsc1 deletion (Slc1a3-CreERT2) does not cause degeneration, and rapamycin treatment after development does not rescue the phenotype.

claim: Retinal rosettes were not seen in Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Mlana-Cre mice.
source: Interestingly, in contrast to Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice, retinal rosettes were not seen in Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Mlana-Cre mice (Figure 3A, third and fifth columns from left), in which Tsc1 was deleted from most of the RPCs by Chx10-EGFP/cre (Chx10-Cre) and from the RPE by Mlana-Cre, respectively (Aydin and Beermann, 2011; Rowan and Cepko, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 3A and references to literature (Aydin and Beermann, 2011; Rowan and Cepko, 2004) describing the Cre expression patterns.

claim: The decrease of MG and retinal rosettes were not found in Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre;Mlana-Cre mouse eyes, in which Tsc1 was deleted in RPC and RPE together.
source: However, we failed to find the decrease of MG as well as retinal rosettes in Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre;Mlana-Cre mouse eyes, in which Tsc1 was deleted in RPC and RPE together (Figure 3A [rightmost column] and 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 3A and quantification in Figure 3B.

claim: The eyes and retinas appeared normal in Tsc1fl/fl;Pax6-aCre mice.
source: However, the eyes and retinas appeared normal in Tsc1fl/fl;Pax6-aCre mice, and their MG cell numbers were not greatly different from those in Tsc1fl/+;Pax6-aCre littermate mice (Figure 4A, third and fourth columns from left).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4A showing normal retinal structure.

claim: Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre mice exhibited normal retinal morphologies and MG cell numbers.
source: However, Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre mice also exhibited normal retinal morphologies and MG cell numbers (Figure 4A, rightmost column).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4A showing normal retinal structure.

claim: The percentages of retinal cells affected by the Cre recombinases in Tsc1fl/+ mouse retinas were approximately 48% for Tyrp1-cre, 65% for Pax6-aCre, 81% for Chx10-Cre, and 92% by Rax-Cre.
source: Our FACS results showed that the percentages of retinal cells affected by the Cre recombinases in Tsc1fl/+ mouse retinas were approximately 48% for Tyrp1-cre, 65% for Pax6-aCre, 81% for Chx10-Cre, and 92% by Rax-Cre.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The cells were increased to about 85% in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas; 89% in Tsc1fl/fl;Pax6-aCre mouse retinas; 93% in Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre mouse retinas; and 95% in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The cells were increased to about 85% in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas; 89% in Tsc1fl/fl;Pax6-aCre mouse retinas; 93% in Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre mouse retinas; and 95% in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: This resulted in 1.77-, 1.36-, 1.16-, and 1.03-fold increases, respectively, of Cre-affected cells in the Tsc1fl/fl;Cre mouse retinas comparing with their littermate Tsc1fl/+;Cre mouse retinas.
source: This resulted in 1.77-, 1.36-, 1.16-, and 1.03-fold increases, respectively, of Cre-affected cells in the Tsc1fl/fl;Cre mouse retinas comparing with their littermate Tsc1fl/+;Cre mouse retinas (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analysis of FACS data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The clonal expansion power of a Tsc1-deficient RPC is inversely correlated with the population of Tsc1-deficient RPCs in developing mouse retina.
source: These results suggest the clonal expansion power of a Tsc1-deficient RPC is inversely correlated with the population of Tsc1-deficient RPCs in developing mouse retina.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that smaller initial Tsc1-deficient populations show greater fold-expansion.

claim: Retinal rosettes were found in the Tsc1f/f;Tyrp1-CreERT2 mice, which were injected with Tam at E9.5, but not in those injected with Tam at P0.
source: We could also find retinal rosettes in the Tsc1f/f;Tyrp1-CreERT2 mice, which were injected with Tam at E9.5, but not in those injected with Tam at P0 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B showing differential phenotypes based on timing of Tsc1 deletion.

claim: Tsc1-deficient RPCs divided faster to form larger neurospheres than those derived from Tsc1-heterozygote RPCs at one post-culture week.
source: We found that Tsc1-deficient RPCs divided faster to form larger neurospheres than those derived from Tsc1-heterozygote RPCs at one post-culture week (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by neurosphere culture data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The Tsc1-deficient neurospheres stopped expanding and the cells comprising the neurospheres started to degenerate after 3 post-culture weeks.
source: However, the Tsc1-deficient neurospheres stopped expanding and the cells comprising the neurospheres started to degenerate after 3 post-culture weeks, while the Tsc1-heterozygote neurospheres expanded slowly and maintained in relative intact forms by 5 post-culture weeks (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by neurosphere culture data shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: The fast expansion and precocious degeneration of Tsc1-deficient neurospheres were not affected by the presence of wild-type neurospheres in the neighbor.
source: The fast expansion and precocious degeneration of Tsc1-deficient neurospheres were not affected by the presence of wild-type neurospheres in the neighbor, suggesting that overproliferation is an intrinsic property of Tsc1-deficient RPCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A – D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-culture experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A-D, demonstrating cell-autonomous effects.

claim: Telomeric DNA sequences are shortened after every cell division unless they are recovered by telomerase.
source: Telomeric DNA sequences are shortened after every cell division unless they are recovered by telomerase (Calado and Dumitriu, 2013; Shay, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature (Calado and Dumitriu, 2013; Shay, 2016).

claim: The average telomere length in mouse retina cells decreased with age.
source: In support of this, we found that the average telomere length in mouse retina cells decreased with age (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The telomere shortening was faster in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: We further found that the telomere shortening was faster in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 5A; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was no significant difference in telomere length between other Tsc1fl/+;Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: However, there was no significant difference in telomere length between other Tsc1fl/+;Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The telomeres in R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient cells of P14 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were significantly shorter than those in R26tdTom-negative neighboring wild-type cells.
source: We found that the telomeres in R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient cells of P14 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were significantly shorter than those in R26tdTom-negative neighboring wild-type cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements of FACS-sorted cells shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The accelerated telomere shortening was observed in the neurospheres derived from Tsc1-deficent RPCs, which were cultured homogenously or together with wild-type neurospheres.
source: The accelerated telomere shortening was also observed in the neurospheres derived from Tsc1-deficent RPCs, which were cultured homogenously or together with wild-type neurospheres (Figure 4—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements in neurosphere cultures shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3F.

claim: Tsc1 deletion had autonomous effects on telomere shortening.
source: These results suggest that Tsc1 deletion had autonomous effects on telomere shortening.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations that telomere shortening occurs specifically in Tsc1-deficient cells even when mixed with wild-type cells.

claim: MG degeneration and retinal rosettes were still observed in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-cre;dTert mouse retinas.
source: However, MG degeneration and retinal rosettes were still observed in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-cre;dTert mouse retinas (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B showing persistent phenotypes despite Tert overexpression.

claim: Telomere shortening is unlikely a direct cause of MG degeneration in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice.
source: This suggests that telomere shortening is unlikely a direct cause of MG degeneration in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Tert overexpression does not rescue the MG degeneration phenotype.

claim: Markers of senescence, including β-galactosidase (β-gal), transformation-related protein 53 (Trp53, p53), p21 cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 A (p21Cip1, p21), and c-Myc were detected in P30 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas but not in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: We found that markers of senescence, including β-galactosidase (β-gal), transformation-related protein 53 (Trp53, p53), p21 cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 A (p21Cip1, p21), and c-Myc (Kuilman et al., 2010), were detected in P30 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas but not in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A, and a citation to literature (Kuilman et al., 2010) defining senescence markers.

claim: β-gal and p53 were enriched more in R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient MG than in R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient AC (Pax6-positive) and BC (Vsx2-positive) populations.
source: Furthermore, β-gal and p53 were enriched more in R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient MG (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 4), which degenerated to form the retinal rosettes (Figure 1C,D), than in R26tdTomato-positive Tsc1-deficient AC (Pax6-positive) and BC (Vsx2-positive) populations, which remained intact in the retinas (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 4, and quantification in Figure 5E.

claim: The senescence markers were increased in Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The senescence markers were also increased in Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B), suggesting that the retinal senescence occurred in an mTORC1-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The senescence markers were not detectable in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre, Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre, and Tsc1fl/fl;Pax6-aCre mouse retinas.
source: In contrast, the senescence markers were not detectable in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre, Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre, and Tsc1fl/fl;Pax6-aCre mouse retinas (Figure 5C), suggesting a positive relationship between RPC clonal expansion power and senescence.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 5C.

claim: Mouse RPCs lacking Rptor were found to exit the cell cycle precociously.
source: In contrast to the accelerated cell cycle progression of Tsc1-deficient RPCs, mouse RPCs lacking Rptor (regulatory-associated protein of mTOR), a key component of mTORC1 (Kim et al., 2002), were found to exit the cell cycle precociously (Choi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature (Kim et al., 2002; Choi et al., 2018) describing Rptor function and phenotypes.

claim: R26tdTom-positive Rptor-deficient cells of P14 Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas had longer telomeres than R26tdTom-negative wild-type neighbors and R26tdTom-positive Rptor-heterozygote cells of Rptorfl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: We found that R26tdTom-positive Rptor-deficient cells of P14 Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas had longer telomeres than R26tdTom-negative wild-type neighbors and R26tdTom-positive Rptor-heterozygote cells of Rptorfl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements of FACS-sorted cells shown in Figure 5H.

claim: There was no significant difference in the telomere lengths of R26tdTom-negative wild-type cells in Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre and Rptorfl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: However, we did not observe a significant difference in the telomere lengths of R26tdTom-negative wild-type cells in Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre and Rptorfl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas, suggesting that there was no compensatory overproliferation of wild-type RPCs after the depletion of Rptor-deficient RPCs in Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements shown in Figure 5H.

claim: There was no increase in the senescence markers in Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: There was also no increase in the senescence markers in Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas, either (Figure 5I and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and immunostaining data in Figure 5I and J.

claim: mTORC1 induces immunoproteasomes to increase the turnover of cyclins and thereby accelerate RPC cell cycle progression.
source: We previously showed that mTORC1 induces immunoproteasomes to increase the turnover of cyclins and thereby accelerate RPC cell cycle progression (Choi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Choi et al., 2018).

claim: Retinal rosettes were absent from approximately a quarter of Psmb8-/-,9-/-,10-/- (Psmb-tko);Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: We found that retinal rosettes were absent from approximately a quarter of in Psmb8-/-,9-/-,10-/- (Psmb-tko);Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas, and R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient retinal clone size was decreased in comparison with that of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A [rightmost column] and 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and quantification in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The level of Hif1a, but not the level of its homolog, Hif2a, was significantly increased in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: We also found that the level of Hif1a, but not the level of its homolog, Hif2a, was significantly increased in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6A.

claim: 96% of Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas did not have rosette structures and MG cell loss.
source: We found that 96% of Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas did not have rosette structures and MG cell loss (Figure 6B [third row] and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 6B and quantification in Figure 6C.

claim: R26tdTom-positive Cre-affected cell population was decreased significantly in Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: R26tdTom-positive Cre-affected cell population was also decreased significantly in Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 6B [second row] and D), suggesting that the hyperexpansion of Tsc1-deficient cell clones was suppressed in these retinas.
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS data in Figure 6D.

claim: The telomere lengths of Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinal cells were increased relative to those of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinal cells.
source: Furthermore, the telomere lengths of Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinal cells were increased relative to those of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinal cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by telomere length measurements shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The levels of the senescence markers induced in degenerating Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were decreased significantly in Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The levels of the senescence markers induced in degenerating Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were also decreased significantly in Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 6A and B [two bottom rows]).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot and immunostaining data in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Hif1a is necessary for the clonal hyperexpansion of Tsc1-deficient cells and the subsequent mitotic aging and senescence-associated degeneration of MG in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina.
source: These results suggest that Hif1a is necessary for the clonal hyperexpansion of Tsc1-deficient cells and the subsequent mitotic aging and senescence-associated degeneration of MG in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue of multiple phenotypes (rosettes, MG loss, clonal expansion, telomere shortening, senescence) by Hif1a deletion.

claim: The numbers of EdU;pH3-positive and CldU;IdU-positive RPCs were significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas in comparison to those in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: We found that the numbers of EdU;pH3-positive and CldU;IdU-positive RPCs were significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas in comparison to those in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 7A [third and seventh rows] and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU/pH3 and CldU/IdU labeling data shown in Figure 7A and quantification in Figure 7C.

claim: The numbers of EdU;Otx2-positive cells, which exited the cell cycle for differentiation to PRs in 12 hr, were increased in the Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The numbers of EdU;Otx2-positive cells, which exited the cell cycle for differentiation to PRs in 12 hr, were also increased in the Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 7A [fifth row] and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU/Otx2 labeling data shown in Figure 7A and quantification in Figure 7C.

claim: The numbers of proliferating cells and the sizes of R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient clones were decreased significantly in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: However, the numbers of proliferating cells and the sizes of R26tdTom-positive Tsc1-deficient clones were decreased significantly in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 7A [right most columns] - C).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation assay data in Figure 7A and quantification in Figure 7B and C.

claim: Hif1a is necessary for the accelerated cell cycle progression of Tsc1-deficient mouse RPCs and consequent expansion of Tsc1-deficient retinal clones.
source: These results therefore suggest that Hif1a is necessary for the accelerated cell cycle progression of Tsc1-deficient mouse RPCs and consequent expansion of Tsc1-deficient retinal clones.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Hif1a deletion reduces proliferation and clonal expansion of Tsc1-deficient cells.

claim: The level of Hif1a protein, but not that of Hif1a mRNA, was increased significantly in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: We found that the level of Hif1a protein, but not that of Hif1a mRNA, was increased significantly in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7D and Western blot data in Figure 7E.

claim: P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were more hypoxic than Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate retinas.
source: We, thus, examined whether a hypoxic condition was established in the mouse retinas using the hypoxyprobe (Varghese et al., 1976), and found that P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were more hypoxic than Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate retinas (Figure 7E and G [bottom row images]).
evidence: The claim is supported by hypoxyprobe staining data shown in Figure 7E and G, and a citation to the hypoxyprobe method (Varghese et al., 1976).

claim: The level of ATP was significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to that in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate control retinas.
source: Interestingly, although hypoxia can compromise mitochondrial ATP synthesis (Vander Heiden et al., 2009), the level of ATP was significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to that in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate control retinas, and it returned to the control level in P0 Hif1afl/fl;Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATP measurements shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, and a citation to literature (Vander Heiden et al., 2009) on hypoxia and mitochondrial function.

claim: The level of lactate was significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas, but not in Hif1afl/fl;Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas.
source: Consistent with this, the level of lactate, which accumulates when glycolysis occurs in a condition of inefficient mitochondrial respiration (Cerychova and Pavlinkova, 2018), was significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas, but not in Hif1afl/fl;Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by lactate measurements shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, and a citation to literature (Cerychova and Pavlinkova, 2018) on lactate accumulation.

claim: Hif1a is necessary for the enhanced glycolysis observed in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: This suggests that Hif1a is necessary for the enhanced glycolysis observed in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that lactate elevation in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre retinas is abolished by Hif1a deletion.

claim: The mRNA and protein levels of glycolytic enzymes (Hk2 and Pkm2) were significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate retinas.
source: We found that the mRNA and protein levels of those glycolytic enzymes were significantly elevated in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas compared to Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate retinas (Figure 7D-F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7D and Western blot data in Figure 7E-F.

claim: The enzyme levels in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were decreased and became similar to those in P0 Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The enzyme levels in P0 Tsc1fl/fl;Hif1afl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas were decreased and became similar to those in P0 Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data in Figure 7D-F showing normalization of glycolytic enzyme levels upon Hif1a deletion.

claim: 2DG treatment decreased the lactate level in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas while metformin increased this parameter.
source: We found that 2DG treatment decreased the lactate level in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas while metformin increased this parameter (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by lactate measurements after drug treatment shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Not only total numbers of CldU-labeled proliferating RPCs but also those that had reentered the cell cycle were decreased significantly in 2DG-treated Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas.
source: We also found that not only total numbers of CldU-labeled proliferating RPCs but also those that had reentered the cell cycle (assessed by monitoring the incorporation of IdU, such that the cells were CldU;IdU-positive) were decreased significantly in 2DG-treated Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas in comparison to the numbers in the PBS- and metformin-injected groups and became similar numbers observed in Tsc1fl/+;Tyrp1-Cre littermate mouse retinas (Figure 7H-J).
evidence: The claim is supported by CldU/IdU labeling data shown in Figure 7H and quantification in Figure 7I-J.

claim: Tsc1-deficient RPCs depend on glycolysis for their accelerated cell cycle progression.
source: These results suggest that Tsc1-deficient RPCs depend on glycolysis for their accelerated cell cycle progression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that glycolysis inhibition (2DG) reduces proliferation of Tsc1-deficient RPCs.

claim: mTORC1 increases the cellular Hif1a protein level through both translational and post-translational mechanisms in the RPCs of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas by generating a hypoxic condition.
source: Collectively, our results suggest that mTORC1 increases the cellular Hif1a protein level through both translational and post-translational mechanisms in the RPCs of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas by generating a hypoxic condition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations: increased Hif1a protein but not mRNA, hypoxia in Tsc1-deficient retinas, and known mechanisms of Hif1a regulation.

claim: Hamartomatous malformation of the CB and iris were reported in human TSC patients and in mice lacking Tsc1 throughout the optic cup.
source: In support of this, hamartomatous malformation of the CB and iris were reported in human TSC patients and in mice lacking Tsc1 throughout the optic cup (Eagle et al., 2000; Hägglund et al., 2017; Milea and Burillon, 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature (Eagle et al., 2000; Hägglund et al., 2017; Milea and Burillon, 1997).

claim: CB/iris malformation was found in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre mice and in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice.
source: We also found CB/iris malformation in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre mice, in which Tsc1 was lost throughout the optic neuroepithelium, and in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice, in which Tsc1 was lost in the RPE, CM, and peripheral retinal clones.
evidence: The claim is based on histological observations described in the text and shown in figures.

claim: CB/iris defects were not observed in mice lacking Tsc1 only in the retina (Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre mice) and RPE (Tsc1fl/fl;Mlana-Cre mice).
source: In contrast, we did not observe CB/iris defects in mice lacking Tsc1 only in the retina (i.e., Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre mice) and RPE (i.e., Tsc1fl/fl;Mlana-Cre mice) (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 3A.

claim: TSC plays an essential role in the CM to generate the CB and iris by suppressing the growth of the areas.
source: This suggests that TSC plays an essential role in the CM to generate the CB and iris by suppressing the growth of the areas.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the pattern of CB/iris defects across different Cre drivers.

claim: The deletion of Tsc2 from the RPE and CM of Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice did not cause CB/iris malformations.
source: However, the deletion of Tsc2 from the RPE and CM of Tsc2fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice did not cause CB/iris malformations, although the mice shared the retinal phenotypes of Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Tsc1 regulates CB and iris development independent of the mTORC1 pathway.
source: These results suggest that Tsc1 regulates CB and iris development independent of the mTORC1 pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential CB/iris phenotypes between Tsc1 and Tsc2 deletion, despite both affecting mTORC1.

claim: Tsc1 functions in the tumor growth factor β (TGFβ)-Smad pathway.
source: Given reported findings that Tsc1 functions in the tumor growth factor β (TGFβ)-Smad pathway (Thien et al., 2015) and the activation of this pathway in mouse CB (Srinivasan et al., 1998), we speculate that Tsc1 might contribute to CB and iris development via the TGFβ-Smad pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature (Thien et al., 2015; Srinivasan et al., 1998).

claim: The CM RPCs in mouse retina were found to proliferate less robustly than the majority RPCs in the central retina.
source: The CM RPCs in mouse retina were found to proliferate less robustly than the majority RPCs in the central retina (Belanger et al., 2017; Marcucci et al., 2016), so did the RPCs in lower vertebrate CMZ (Harris and Perron, 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature (Belanger et al., 2017; Marcucci et al., 2016; Harris and Perron, 1998).

claim: The CM RPCs could have a competitive advantage for clonal expansion over the majority wild-type RPCs when their cell cycle progression is accelerated by losing Tsc1.
source: However, the CM RPCs could have a competitive advantage for clonal expansion over the majority wild-type RPCs, which divide and expand slowly, when their cell cycle progression is accelerated by losing Tsc1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the model shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and the observed clonal expansion patterns.

claim: The competitive clonal expansion of a Tsc1-deficient RPC exceeding the division limit did not occur in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre mouse retinas.
source: The competitive hyperexpansion of a Tsc1-deficient RPC exceeding the division limit did not occur in Tsc1fl/fl;Rax-Cre and Tsc1fl/fl;Chx10-Cre mouse retinas, since its neighboring RPCs also lose Tsc1 and expand as fast as the RPC (Figures 4C and 5A; Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the FACS and telomere data in Figures 4C and 5A, and the model in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Wild-type RPCs in the Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina did not overproliferate even though their neighboring Rptor-deficient RPCs stopped expanding their clones.
source: However, wild-type RPCs in the Rptorfl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina did not overproliferate even though their neighboring Rptor-deficient RPCs stopped expanding their clones (Figure 5F–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by data in Figure 5F-J showing no change in wild-type cell telomere length or expansion.

claim: The overproliferation might be a specific feature of Tsc1-deficient RPC but not a relative property obtained by the division differences.
source: Therefore, the overproliferation might be a specific feature of Tsc1-deficient RPC but not a relative property obtained by the division differences.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison between Tsc1-deficient and Rptor-deficient scenarios.

claim: The MG are among the last-born retinal cell types, arising around the first postnatal week in mice.
source: The MG are among the last-born retinal cell types, arising around the first postnatal week in mice (Cepko, 2014; Hoang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature (Cepko, 2014; Hoang et al., 2020).

claim: RPCs producing MG are likely to be mitotically older than those producing other retinal cell types.
source: Therefore, given the specific temporal sequence of retinal histogenesis, RPCs producing MG are likely to be mitotically older than those producing other retinal cell types.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal sequence of retinal cell type production.

claim: Among the last-born retinal cell types, only MG exhibited significant degeneration in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina.
source: Among the last-born retinal cell types, only MG exhibited significant degeneration in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retina (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data in Figure 1D showing selective MG loss.

claim: The MG might be in less terminal stage than the other last-born types (i.e., rPR and BC) in terms of differentiation.
source: The MG might be in less terminal stage than the other last-born types (i.e., rPR and BC) in terms of differentiation, since they can resume cell cycle to regenerate neurons in the injured cold-blooded vertebrate retinas (Lahne et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to literature (Lahne et al., 2020) on MG regenerative capacity.

claim: Mouse MG could divide after injury if histone deacetylase inhibitor is provided after viral expression of achaete-scute homolog 1.
source: Mouse MG could also divide after the injury, if histone deacetylase inhibitor is provided after viral expression of a proneural transcription factor achaete-scute homolog 1 (Jorstad et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to literature (Jorstad et al., 2017).

claim: Telomere shortening in mouse cells is rarely associated with deleterious effects because the mouse telomere is 5–10 times longer than the human telomere.
source: Furthermore, unlike the strong relationship between telomere shortening and senescence in human cells, telomere shortening in mouse cells is rarely associated with deleterious effects because the mouse telomere is 5–10 times longer than the human telomere (Calado and Dumitriu, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to literature (Calado and Dumitriu, 2013).

claim: The activation of mTORC1 by Tsc1 deletion was shown to cause premature aging in mouse intestinal stem cells (ISCs).
source: The activation of mTORC1 by Tsc1 deletion was also shown to cause premature aging in mouse intestinal stem cells (ISCs) (He et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to literature (He et al., 2020).

claim: The aging of Tsc1-deficient ISCs was reported to mediate the stress-induced p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, which activates p53 to block ISC proliferation.
source: The aging of Tsc1-deficient ISCs was reported to mediate the stress-induced p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway, which activates p53 to block ISC proliferation.
evidence: The claim is based on information from the cited literature on ISC aging mechanisms.

claim: The activation of p38 MAPK was observed in all four Tsc1-cko mouse retinas.
source: We also observed the activation (i.e., phosphorylation) of p38 MAPK in all four Tsc1-cko mouse retinas (data not shown), whereas senescence occurred only in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mouse retinas (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on unpublished data mentioned in the text and comparison with senescence data in Figure 5C.

claim: Trp53fl/fl;Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice still exhibited MG degeneration and retinal rosette formation.
source: The activation of p53 did not likely cause degeneration of Tsc1-deficient RPCs and/or MG, either, since Trp53fl/fl;Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice still exhibited MG degeneration and retinal rosette formation (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on unpublished data mentioned in the text.

claim: Intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) derived from Tsc1-deficient ISCs were degenerated via receptor interacting protein kinase 3 (Ripk3)-mediated necroptosis.
source: A previous study further showed that intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) derived from Tsc1-deficient ISCs were degenerated via receptor interacting protein kinase 3 (Ripk3)-mediated necroptosis (Xie et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to literature (Xie et al., 2020).

claim: The MG degeneration in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice was not blocked by concomitant deletion of Ripk3.
source: However, in contrast to the critical roles of Ripk3 in the degeneration of Tsc1-deficient IECs, the MG degeneration in Tsc1fl/fl;Tyrp1-Cre mice was not blocked by concomitant deletion of Ripk3 (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on unpublished data mentioned in the text.

claim: Embryonic and neonatal mouse retinas receive oxygen that diffuses from the distant hyaloid vessels in the vitreous and the choroid vessels across the RPE.
source: Embryonic and neonatal mouse retinas receive oxygen that diffuses from the distant hyaloid vessels in the vitreous and the choroid vessels across the RPE, whereas the mature mouse retina has close access to the oxygen released from intraretinal blood vessels (Lutty and McLeod, 2018; Saint-Geniez and D'amore, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature (Lutty and McLeod, 2018; Saint-Geniez and D'amore, 2004).

claim: RPCs in the inner embryonic mouse retinas are farthest from the vessels, and are likely to exist under more hypoxic conditions than cells adjacent to the vitreous and RPE.
source: RPCs in the inner embryonic mouse retinas are farthest from the vessels, and are likely to exist under more hypoxic conditions than cells adjacent to the vitreous and RPE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the spatial relationship between RPCs and oxygen sources.

claim: The inner RPCs might adapt to use glycolysis ATP synthesis than oxygen-dependent mitochondrial ATP synthesis for proper proliferation, as has been suggested for Xenopus retina.
source: The inner RPCs therefore might adapt to use glycolysis ATP synthesis than oxygen-dependent mitochondrial ATP synthesis for proper proliferation, as has been suggested for Xenopus retina (Agathocleous et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is speculative, supported by analogy to Xenopus retina (Agathocleous et al., 2012).
